item.description:

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Tue Sep 1 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Edouard, located over the northwestern Gulf of America.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Edouard are issued under WMO
header WTNT35 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Edouard are issued under WMO
header WTNT25 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT5.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard Public Advisory Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 1000 AM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026 
147 
WTNT35 KNHC 011445
TCPAT5
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Edouard Advisory Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
1000 AM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026
 
...AIR FORCE HURRICANE HUNTERS FIND EDOUARD IS STRENGTHENING...
...CONTINUED INTENSIFICATION IS EXPECTED BEFORE EDOUARD REACHES THE
NORTHWESTERN GULF COAST TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1000 AM CDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.4N 93.3W
ABOUT 30 MI...45 KM S OF CAMERON LOUISIANA
ABOUT 50 MI...80 KM SE OF PORT ARTHUR TEXAS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Storm Surge Warning is in effect for...
* High Island, Texas to the Vermilion/Cameron Parish Line
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* High Island, Texas to Cameron, Louisiana
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Port Bolivar, Texas to the Vermilion/Iberia Parish Line
 
A Storm Surge Warning means there is a danger of life-threatening
inundation, from rising water moving inland from the coastline,
during the next 12 to 24 hours in the indicated locations. For a
depiction of areas at risk, please see the National Weather Service
Storm Surge Watch/Warning Graphic, available at hurricanes.gov. This
is a life-threatening situation. Persons located within these areas
should take all necessary actions to protect life and property from
rising water and the potential for other dangerous conditions.
Promptly follow evacuation and other instructions from local
officials.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area, in this case within the next 6 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within the
next 6 to 12 hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area, including possible
inland watches and warnings, please monitor products issued by your
local National Weather Service forecast office.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1000 AM CDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Edouard was
located near latitude 29.4 North, longitude 93.3 West. Edouard is
moving toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue through early Wednesday. On the forecast 
track, the center of Edouard is forecast to reach the northwestern 
Gulf Coast within the warning area later today and move inland over 
southeast Texas tonight.
 
Data from the Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunters indicate that 
maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Additional strengthening is forecast before Edouard makes landfall 
today, and the storm could approach hurricane strength. Rapid 
weakening is expected after the center moves inland.
 
Edouard is a small tropical cyclone. Tropical-storm-force winds 
extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Storm Edouard can be found in the
Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT5 and WMO
header WTNT45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions will spread over portions of the
warning area during the next few hours. Hurricane conditions
are possible within the Hurricane Watch area later today.
 
STORM SURGE: The combination of storm surge and tide will cause
normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by rising waters
moving inland from the shoreline. The water could reach the
following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated areas if
the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide...
 
High Island, TX to Vermilion/Cameron Parish Line, LA...3-5 ft
Vermilion/Cameron Parish Line, LA to Morgan City, LA...1-3 ft
 
The deepest water will occur along the immediate coast near and to
the right of the center. Surge-related flooding depends on the
relative timing of the surge and the tidal cycle, and can vary
greatly over short distances. For information specific to your
area, please see products issued by your local National Weather
Service forecast office.
 
For a complete depiction of areas at risk of storm surge inundation,
please see the National Weather Service Peak Storm Surge Graphic,
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?peakSurge.
 
RAINFALL: Edouard is expected to produce rainfall totals of 3 to 6
inches with maximum totals up to 9 inches for parts of the Upper
Texas Coast inland through east-central Texas, with potential for 2
to 4 inches in far southwest Louisiana. This rainfall is likely to
produce flash flooding, especially in low-lying and urban areas.
River flooding may also be possible.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Edouard, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total
Rainfall Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?ero.
 
TORNADOES: A tornado or two is possible this afternoon and evening
over parts of southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 100 PM CDT.
Next complete advisory at 400 PM CDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 400 AM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTNT45 KNHC 010848
TCDAT5
 
Tropical Storm Edouard Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
400 AM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026
 
It has been easy to track the center of Edouard this morning, 
showing up as a well-defined core of shallow convection on shortwave 
infrared satellite imagery and radar reflectivity from Lake Charles, 
Louisiana (KLCH). While the final fixes from the prior Air Force 
Reserve reconnaissance mission did not show an additional pressure 
drop, their remarks did note a nascent low-level eyewall was trying 
to form, which can also be seen from land-based radar. This 
structure could prove important for Edouard's near-term 
intensification prospects as deep convection begins to reform close 
to the storm center. For now, the initial intensity remains 35 kt 
this advisory, in agreement with radial velocity data from KLCH and 
the 06 UTC TAFB Dvorak intensity estimate. Another Air Force Reserve 
reconnaissance mission is scheduled to investigate Edouard again 
this morning. 
 
The intensity forecast today is problematic. Edouard has managed to 
develop a small core that could be prone to rapid changes in 
intensity. In addition, environmental conditions are quite favorable 
for intensification while Edouard remains over water, with 31 C 
sea-surface temperatures, and low vertical wind shear diagnosed at  
4 kt by UW-CIMSS. The raw output from the hurricane-regional models 
responds to these factors by showing substantial intensification 
today, with both HMON and HAFS-A making Edouard a hurricane before 
landfall. HAFS-B and HWRF show a somewhat more tempered rate of 
intensification. Given Edouard's current structure, a rapid 
increase in intensity before landfall is still anticipated, and the 
latest NHC forecast shows a 55 kt intensity near landfall, which is 
close to the raw model HAFS-B output at that time. Of note, this is 
well above the interpolated intensity guidance which can struggle 
to depict rapid short-term intensity changes in these cases close 
to landfall. After landfall, Edouard should quickly weaken, likely 
becoming post-tropical in 36 h and dissipating by 48 h. 
 
Edouard continues to move off to the west-northwest at 300/7 kt. A 
prominent low- to mid-level ridge centered over the southeastern 
United States should continue to steer the tropical cyclone to the 
west-northwest then turning more northwest after 24 h as the storm 
rounds the ridge. On this track, Edouard should make landfall later 
today near the Louisiana/Texas border, and then push inland over 
eastern Texas by tonight. The track guidance remains in good 
agreement, though with just a slight westward shift, and the NHC 
track forecast is just a touch west of the previous advisory, 
closest to the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA).
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Edouard is expected to strengthen and it could approach hurricane
strength before it reaches the northwest Gulf Coast later today.
Tropical Storm conditions are expected along the northwest Gulf
Coast with hurricane conditions possible from High Island to
Cameron.
 
2. A Storm Surge Warning is in effect from High Island, Texas to
the Vermilion/Cameron Parish Line, Louisiana where peak values of
3 to 5 feet above ground level are possible along the immediate
coast within the warning area.
 
3. Heavy rain will impact parts of the Upper Texas coast through
east-central Texas into far Southwest Louisiana today and
tomorrow as Tropical Storm Edouard tracks inland. Flash flooding is
likely across this region, especially in urban areas. River flooding
may also be possible.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  01/0900Z 29.0N  92.8W   35 KT  40 MPH
 12H  01/1800Z 29.7N  93.8W   55 KT  65 MPH...ON THE COAST
 24H  02/0600Z 30.6N  95.0W   30 KT  35 MPH...INLAND
 36H  02/1800Z 31.7N  95.9W   20 KT  25 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 48H  03/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Papin
